videos.title: Eat This Before Bed — Watch What Happens to Your Belly Overnight | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Eat This Before Bed — Watch What Happens to Your Belly Overnight | Dr. Mandell What you eat before bed can influence hunger, satiety, overnight protein availability, and how hungry you feel when you wake up. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell shows you a simple three-ingredient bedtime combination built around slow-digesting protein that may be especially useful for people who struggle with nighttime hunger, late-night snacking, or waking up hungry. The combination starts with about 1/2 cup of low-fat or 2% cottage cheese, which is naturally rich in casein, a slowly digested dairy protein that provides amino acids over an extended period. Add approximately 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon and, if appropriate for your diet, a very small pinch of salt. Eat it approximately 45–60 minutes before bedtime rather than immediately before lying down, particularly if you're prone to reflux. Pre-sleep protein has been studied in relation to overnight protein synthesis and recovery, while higher-protein foods can also promote satiety and may help some people better control appetite. Cinnamon has also been studied for its potential effects on glucose metabolism, although it should not be viewed as a treatment for diabetes or as a way to prevent fat storage from a meal. Most importantly, this bedtime snack does not magically burn belly fat while you sleep. Changes in body fat ultimately depend on your overall energy intake, activity, sleep, metabolic health, and dietary pattern over time. However, if nighttime hunger repeatedly leads you to snack on highly processed, calorie-dense foods, a planned protein-rich option may make it easier to control those nighttime calories and maintain a healthier eating pattern. If you're lactose intolerant, lactose-free cottage cheese may be an option; if you have a dairy allergy, this approach isn't appropriate. People who have been instructed to restrict sodium, protein, or dairy because of a medical condition should follow their healthcare professional's recommendations. And if nighttime hunger is severe, persistent, or associated with unusual thirst, urination, unexplained weight changes, or other symptoms, discuss it with your healthcare professional. Try it and pay attention to your hunger, sleep comfort, and appetite the following morning.

videos.title: OpenAI’s GPT-7 Leaked: 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Leap
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s GPT-7 Leaked: 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Leap https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

More than 10 trillion parameters. An alleged secret OpenAI pretraining run called “Bel.” And a wave of posts claiming GPT-7 is enormous, nearly finished, possibly AGI-level, and coming before the end of 2026.

There’s one major problem: the original leak never says GPT-7. Not once.

The entire GPT-7 rumor cycle traces largely back to an August 25, 2026 post from the X account “leo” (@synthwavedd), which claimed OpenAI had completed a massive pretrain codenamed Bel — supposedly the successor to another internal project called Doug. The post described Bel as having more than 10 trillion total parameters and potentially serving as a post-GPT-6 foundation.

That is very different from saying OpenAI has a finished 10-trillion-parameter model called GPT-7.

OpenAI has filed an intent-to-use US trademark application for “GPT-7,” but a trademark reserves a name; it doesn’t confirm a product, specification, price, or release date. OpenAI’s public documentation currently stops at the GPT-6 family, with GPT-6 Astra beginning its rollout on September 3, 2026.

Even Sam Altman’s widely shared “$0 GPT-7” comment is far less significant than it sounds. The line comes from a joking reply from December 2023 — not a GPT-7 announcement or pricing commitment.

And that’s where this gets interesting.

The 10 trillion parameter claim has been repeated across coverage, but it still traces back to the Bel post. Even if the figure is accurate, “total parameters” doesn’t automatically tell you how expensive or capable a model is. A mixture-of-experts architecture can contain an enormous total parameter count while activating only a fraction for each token. OpenAI also doesn’t publicly disclose parameter counts for models such as GPT-5.6 or GPT-6 Astra.

So the viral claim that “GPT-7 has 10 trillion parameters” requires at least two assumptions: that Bel really exists and has the reported size, and that Bel is actually GPT-7.

Then the story gets even messier.

Claims that GPT-7 is already available, will launch by the end of 2026, will be free, coordinates sub-agents for days, has leaked early-access code, or has been confirmed as AGI all fall apart when traced back to their original sources. Some supposed GPT-7 features appear to be capabilities already associated with GPT-6 Astra. Other screenshots, demos, repositories, and quotes are unsupported, mislabeled, or fake.

But Bel can’t simply be dismissed either. The same account reportedly leaked the intermediate GPT-5.5 model in late 2025 before it became known publicly. That gives the source some precedent — but it doesn’t independently verify Bel, Doug, the 10 trillion figure, or any connection to GPT-7.

Meanwhile, there are real OpenAI developments worth paying attention to.

GPT-5.6 launched on July 10, 2026 in Sol, Terra, and Luna variants alongside ChatGPT Work. OpenAI reported GPT-5.6 Sol scoring 73.5% on ExploitBench, compared with 47.9% for GPT-5.5.

Then came GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI reports Astra reaching 98% on FrontierMath, 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3, and 100% on ExploitBench. On OSWorld, Astra reportedly reached 72.6% in roughly 40 minutes versus GPT-5.6 at 65.7% in around 75 minutes. These are OpenAI’s own reported results, not independent verification.

Astra’s safety results are equally interesting. On an internal evaluation testing whether a model takes unauthorized actions outside its assigned scope.

Paul Maurice Talks About Brad Marchand Injury, Florida Panthers Beat LA Kings Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice talks after his team’s 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. 

The Panthers (2-0-2) play their home opener on Saturday against the Minnesota Wild. 

Florida, which already lost captain Sasha Barkov to injury, appear to have lost Brad Marchand as well after he was helped off the ice in the second period. He went down and was clutching his left knee. 

The Panthers trailed 1-0 in the first but tied the score in the second on a goal from Seth Jones. Matthew Tkachuk gave Florida its first regulation lead of the season in the third. Jacob Markstrom got another win and is 2-0-1 thus far.

Does it seem like water isn’t quenching your thirst? There are two main reasons this can happen: You may not be drinking enough fluid, or you may have low blood volume. Low blood volume is the more common scenario.

Low blood volume is one of the most common causes of excessive thirst. Drinking more water can actually make the problem worse, leaving you with constant thirst.

To retain enough fluid and maintain healthy blood volume, you need adequate salt.

Low sodium and low blood volume symptoms include:
• Feeling dizzy or unstable when standing up quickly
• Persistent thirst, especially at night
• Fatigue, weak muscles, or cramping
• Poor sleep
• Headaches
• Feeling cold
• Constipation
• Dark urine
• Dry mouth and dry eyes

You need around 3000 to 4000 mg of sodium each day to maintain healthy hydration levels. This is equal to about 1½ to 2 teaspoons of salt per day. If you’re an athlete or physically active, you may need more.

videos.title: New Jaguar Type 01: My HONEST take…
videos.summary_source_text:
New Jaguar Type 01: My HONEST take… Meet the most anticipated car of the year - the new Jaguar Type 01! 

Explore new & used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-0710

The Jaguar Type 01 has been unveiled! 

It’s been almost two years since Jaguar showed the Type 00 concept car to the public, and it’s fair to say the production car looks remarkably similar to the concept! 

Jaguar was aiming for a full reset with the Type 00 concept. The question is, does the production car help it achieve its goal? Let’s take a closer look… 

The similarities to the Type 00 Concept are clear. For starters, it’s absolutely colossal! It has a huge bonnet, and the car measures 5.2 metres long. Along the front you’ll find thin headlights and DRLs, as well as a bumper that features active aero to help the Type 01 cool when required.  The ‘grille’ includes the same lines as seen on the concept, along with Jaguar’s all-new logo. From the side, you’ll find 23-inch alloys that come as standard, four doors (unlike the two seen on the concept), and pop-out door handles. Around the back, the slat design continues across the entire rear end, with two full-length light bars built into them. There’s also a pop-up spoiler when the car hits high speed, and perhaps most notably, there’s no rear window!

On the inside, the interior of the Type 01 is incredibly minimalistic. There’s a large central spine that runs from the front to the rear (so it’s strictly a four-door), and there’s a small infotainment screen to manage the climate controls. There’s a large digital dial screen that’s touch-sensitive, and the steering wheel is modern and comes with buttons to control the dial screen. There’s a sound bar that runs along the length of the windscreen, with speakers built into the seat headrests. 

A car of this size needs a lot of power, so it’s no surprise it comes equipped with three electric motors - one at the front and two at the rear. The three combine to produce 1,030hp and 1,365Nm, with a claimed 0-60 time of 4 seconds. That may seem slow for a car with so much power, but then again, it does weigh around 2.7 tonnes! 

We don’t have an official price yet, but don’t be surprised to find it any cheaper than £120,000! So do you think it’s worth it? Let us know in the comments!

videos.summary_source_text:
06.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Hindi - 06.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 06.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

videos.title: How to Stop Waking Up to Pee At Night
videos.summary_source_text:
How to Stop Waking Up to Pee At Night If you’re dealing with frequent urination at night, the problem is not your bladder.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4xPOE4t

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Approximately 1 in 5 men and 1 in 4 women in the U.S. get up at least once or twice to urinate every night. Waking up to pee, even just once, can wreck your sleep and wreak havoc on your health!

So what’s really causing this widespread issue? The antidiuretic hormone (ADH) plays a crucial role in preventing excessive urination. A problem with this hormone affects water balance, causing you to produce more urine, especially at night.

Too much salt and not enough potassium, blood sugar issues, and insulin resistance all affect ADH and can cause you to produce more urine to eliminate excess salt and sugar.

Dmitry Kulikov, Florida Panthers Morning Skate at LA Kings Florida Panthers defenseman Dmitry Kulikov meets the media after his team’s morning skate in Los Angeles on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. 

The Panthers (1-0-2) are coming off a 3-2 loss in OT to the host Anaheim Ducks on Sunday. 

On Sunday, the Panthers got Brad Marchand back for the first time since March after putting captain Sasha Barkov on LTIR. 

Down 2-1 late in the second, the Panthers got the game-tying goal from Marchand with 1:50 left. Carter Verhaeghe tied the score at 1 in the first. 

Florida wraps up the road trip Tuesday against the Los Angeles Kings at 10 (ESPN).

Press This Spot for 60 Seconds Before Bed — Watch What Happens | Dr. Mandell Before you close your eyes tonight, try this simple 60-second technique designed to help your body settle down and prepare for a more restful night. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell shows you a specific area in the arch of the foot and demonstrates how to gently massage it using your thumb for just one minute before bed. Your feet contain thousands of sensory nerve endings and receptors, and gentle foot massage can provide calming sensory input while helping release muscular tension and encouraging relaxation as part of your nighttime routine. You’ll learn exactly where to place your thumb, how much pressure to use, and how to make small circular movements while allowing your body and mind to unwind. Although this area has traditionally been described as a reflexology point, reflexology claims linking individual points on the foot to specific internal organs or hormones have not been conclusively established by scientific research. The benefit of this technique is better viewed as a simple form of massage, sensory stimulation, and relaxation that may help some people transition from the activity and stress of the day toward sleep. Quality sleep is essential because many important restorative processes occur during normal sleep, including tissue recovery, memory consolidation, metabolic regulation, and normal brain waste-clearance activity. Try this for 60 seconds tonight and pay attention to how your body responds. You may notice your feet feel warmer, your muscles feel less tense, or you simply feel more relaxed and ready for sleep. Never press hard enough to cause pain, and avoid massaging an injured, infected, swollen, or otherwise medically concerning area of the foot. If you have significant neuropathy, impaired sensation, circulation problems, or another medical condition affecting your feet, speak with your healthcare professional before trying new massage techniques. Small bedtime habits can make a meaningful difference in how relaxed you feel going into the night.

videos.title: Gemini 5 Is Here: Google's 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 5 Is Here: Google's 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Gemini 5 is supposedly Google’s next monster AI model: trillion-scale parameters, a 10-million-token context window, and maybe even something approaching AGI. There’s just one problem — Google has never officially announced Gemini 5.

No launch. No confirmed specs. No benchmark scores. And no public confirmation from Google DeepMind, Sundar Pichai, Demis Hassabis, Jeff Dean, or Gemini lead Koray Kavukcuoglu that a model called “Gemini 5” even exists.

Meanwhile, Google’s actual next-generation model — Gemini 4 Argon — is already making some extraordinary claims of its own.

Google’s AI release cadence helps explain why the Gemini 5 rumors spread so quickly. Gemini 2.5 Pro arrived in March 2025 with a million-token input window. Gemini 3 followed in November 2025, integrated directly into Google Search’s AI Mode. Gemini 3.5 Flash arrived in May 2026 with a stronger focus on agentic AI. Just four months later came Gemini 4 Argon.

But a fast release cycle isn’t proof that Gemini 5 is around the corner.

Argon itself is the more interesting story. Google demonstrated the model translating an 800,000-line C/C++ Fuchsia OS codebase into Rust while preserving functionality. Google also says Argon improved a quantum scheduling algorithm by 40% over the previous baseline.

Then there are the benchmarks.

The MOST Dangerous Carbs in the World! The most dangerous carbs are highly refined starches that break down rapidly into glucose and can spike blood sugar and insulin more than actual sugar. 

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/3VoI33B

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Watch for these common forms of industrial starch:

* Maltodextrin
* Modified food starch
* Cornstarch
* Tapioca starch
* Wheat starch
* Refined rice flour

These ingredients are commonly used in processed foods and can be easy to overlook because they aren’t always labeled as sugar.

videos.summary_source_text:
485. Prata pengar med barnen: rättvisa, tillit och fallgropar | Med Moa Diseborn Hur pratar man med barnen om arv? Sju av tio förmögenhetsöverföringar misslyckas, och sällan på grund av pengarna. 

Jag pratar med beteendevetaren Moa Diseborn om barn, arv och nästa generation, temat som vann omröstningen på vårt senaste flocken-event för dig med god ekonomi.

Vi går igenom riktiga fall från forumet: föräldrarna som fejkade fattigdom, hästen som kostar 15 000 kronor i månaden när syskonet nöjer sig med badbyxor, förskottet på arv som ingen berättade om och arvtagare som förlamas av tacksamhetsskuld. Moa förklarar varför pengar är en förstärkare, vad pedagogisk fallhöjd betyder för ekonomin och varför juridik kan vara kärlek.

videos.title: 05.10.26 - Ep.25 (Part 2) - The Risk Spectrum: Capital Moves Between Safety and Opportunity
videos.summary_source_text:
05.10.26 - Ep.25 (Part 2) - The Risk Spectrum: Capital Moves Between Safety and Opportunity Capital is always moving.

In Part 2, we continue from Episode 24 and examine how capital moves through the global financial system — and why those movements matter to markets.

THE RISK SPECTRUM

Capital constantly moves between lower-risk environments focused on capital preservation and higher-risk environments focused on growth, leverage and opportunity.

Those decisions are influenced by:

• Interest rates
• Inflation
• Economic expectations
• Market volatility
• Credit conditions
• Liquidity
• Valuations
• Investor confidence

In a risk-on environment, capital may seek equities, growth stocks, high-yield credit, emerging markets, commodities, crypto and other higher-volatility opportunities.

In a risk-off environment, capital may move toward cash, high-quality government debt, defensive assets and liquidity.

But there is no single definition of “risk” for every participant.

CAPITAL HAS DIFFERENT OBJECTIVES

A pension fund may prioritise stability. An insurer may match future liabilities. A bank may prioritise liquidity. A hedge fund may use capital for positions and hedging. A corporation may need working capital. A sovereign wealth fund may pursue strategic objectives. A market maker may manage inventory and exposure.

When financing is readily available and confidence is strong, businesses and investors may increase borrowing, investment and risk-taking.

When financial conditions tighten, the process can reverse.

Liquidity can appear abundant during normal conditions — until everyone wants it at the same time.

During periods of stress, investors may sell assets simultaneously, spreads can widen, volatility can increase and leveraged positions can be unwound.

A leveraged investor may be forced to sell an attractive asset because of margin requirements or collateral pressure.

Where is it leaving?

Where is it going?

Why is the destination becoming relatively more attractive?

NEW 850hp Polestar 5 proves you DON’T NEED a PORSCHE! Should the German market leader be worried about this all-new Polestar?!

Get 20% off Car Vertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

Meet the all-new Polestar 5! 

It’s an all-electric performance GT that has class leaders like the Audi e-tron GT & Porsche Taycan in its sights! 

The question is, does the Polestar offer enough to steer you away from the more established, best-in-class models that Germany has to offer? Let’s take a closer look… 

In terms of the design, there’s no denying it has some real presence on the road. Up front, it comes with split headlight elements that really help it look menacing. You’ll find some fake vents at the front, although there’s a large vent across the bottom of the bumper that can close when the battery doesn’t need cooling. The safety sensors have also been well hidden, to further improve the looks. Along the side, there are contours on the doors to add more definition, coupled with frameless windows. The pop-out door handles may not be to everyone’s taste, but thankfully, both the front and rear doors have soft-close. Around the rear, the futuristic design cues continue, and the main statement here is a lack of a rear window!

On the inside, you’ll find similar Scandinavian minimalism as found in other Polestar cars - but that’s no bad thing! There are soft-touch, high-quality materials throughout the cabin, and the centre console is dominated by a large vertical infotainment screen. There are no physical buttons, so everything is managed through the screen, but thankfully the system is crisp and quick to use. The digital dials are easy to manage with buttons on the steering wheel, which is of a good size. It also comes with damped, high-quality stalks on either side. 

The Polestar 5 comes with some serious power. All options come with two motors, with the entry-level being able to produce 748hp. If you choose the Performance version, this output is significantly boosted to 884hp! It’s powered by a 106kWh battery, and the Performance edition has a range of 416 miles. 

But of course, all of this performance and power doesn’t come cheap. The Polestar 5 starts from £89,000, rising to £105,000 for the Performance edition. However, the car we’re reviewing here, with all options added, costs £117,000! 

So would you really choose one of these over a Porsche? Let us know in the comments!

Do This To Become A Top Scorer In 1 Season The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

📱 Download the Swing Coach App (2-Week Free Trial) → https://go.meandmygolf.com/swingcoach/yt/?utm_source=YouTube&utm_medium=Description&utm_campaign=05.10.26

Hunter is a scratch golfer with a great-looking golf swing, but he was still struggling with an over-the-top move that was affecting both his iron strike and direction.

In this live golf lesson, Piers identifies that the problem wasn’t simply in Hunter’s downswing. It began much earlier.

Hunter wasn’t turning and loading effectively into his trail leg during the backswing. Instead, his body was moving towards the target and leaving him in a position where shallowing the club became extremely difficult.

The lesson had two important stages. First, Piers helped Hunter improve how he turned and loaded his right side in the backswing. They then worked on the lower-body movement and upper-body tilt needed to deliver the club from a shallower position.

The difference was clear: a better downswing, improved contact and flushed draws.

If you struggle with coming over the top, this lesson shows why the downswing might not be the best place to start.

Is it really all in the hips, like the famous line from Caddyshack? What if it's actually your wrists?

If you are interested in HackMotion:  https://hackmotion.com/affiliates/alitaylorgolf/?aff=9&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=affiliate&utm_campaign=alitaylorgolf&utm_content=pp&utm_term=02_10_2026

In this video I show you what causes thin and fat shots and how to fix it, using HackMotion wrist data and TrackMan numbers to see exactly what's happening.

In this video you'll see:
✅ How an over-extended lead wrist at the top opens the clubface and sets up an early release
✅ Why that leaves you scooping at the ball and hitting it thin or fat

✅ How keeping your hands ahead of the ball gives you a neutral face and path

videos.summary_source_text:
I'm 51. This is What I Eat EVERY Day to Be Lean. Want to know what to eat to get shredded, build muscle, and stay lean all year? In this video, I’m sharing 12 foods I eat every day that make my diet easier to follow and help me maintain six pack abs without giving up the foods I enjoy.

Get Lean and Stay Lean Here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe to this channel here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

If you’ve been looking for the Jeff Cavaliere diet plan or wondering how to eat like ATHLEAN-X, this is a look at the foods behind my daily eating plan. I’ll explain what I eat, why I choose it, and how these foods fit into a muscle building diet that supports hard training while keeping calories under control.

Getting lean takes more than finding the right foods. Your total calories, protein intake, workouts, and consistency all matter. But choosing meals that satisfy your appetite and taste good makes it easier to stick with your nutrition plan long enough to see results.

Here are some of the foods I rely on every day.

My breakfast starts with egg whites. They give me a convenient source of protein without adding many calories or much fat. When your goal is to get ripped while maintaining muscle, having an easy way to include protein at breakfast helps you start the day on track. Egg whites also leave room for other foods in the meal without making it difficult to manage your overall calorie intake.

Oatmeal is another staple of my daily meal plan. It provides carbohydrates to fuel my workouts, along with fiber that helps make breakfast more satisfying. I use plain oatmeal so I can control what goes into it instead of relying on varieties with added sugar. If you’re wondering what to eat to be lean, a breakfast you enjoy and can prepare consistently is a great place to start.

I drink skim milk with breakfast and use it in my oatmeal and protein shake later in the day. It supplies protein and calcium while keeping calories lower than the same amount of whole milk. Because I consume it several times throughout the day, that difference helps me keep my diet aligned with my goals. I also choose milk fortified with vitamins A and D.

Cinnamon is a simple addition that makes my oatmeal taste better without needing a lot of added sugar. That matters because a diet for abs should include meals you look forward to eating. Small choices that improve flavor can make a healthy eating plan easier to repeat, and repetition is a big part of staying lean year-round.

Greek yogurt is one of my go-to lunch foods because it’s convenient, versatile, and high in protein. It already contains all nine essential amino acids, making it a complete protein source. I like adding chia or pumpkin seeds for extra texture and nutrients. Pay attention to the variety you choose, since protein, calories, and added sugar can vary between products.

I’ve said plenty of times that I have a sweet tooth. Instead of expecting that to disappear, I make room for a dessert I enjoy. For me, that means a portion of frozen yogurt that fits my daily calorie intake. The amount and toppings matter. Having six pack abs doesn’t require eliminating dessert, but it does require being aware of how those choices fit into your overall diet.

Chicken, fish, and lean cuts of red meat are regular parts of my eating plan. I typically build my main meals around a serving that provides approximately 30–50 grams of protein. Getting enough protein helps support muscle growth and maintenance, making it a priority whether I’m focused on building muscle or staying lean. Different seasonings and preparation methods keep these meals from becoming repetitive.

Yes, I eat pasta. Carbohydrates have a place in a meal plan to get ripped, especially when you’re training hard and want to support your performance. Pasta gives me a food I enjoy and a practical source of workout fuel. Portion size and what you add to it matter. I make it fit my nutrition goals instead of assuming I need to cut it out to get a six pack.

Vegetables like broccoli help round out my meals with fiber, vitamins, and minerals. They also add volume to my plate, which can make a meal more satisfying when I’m managing calories. A muscle building nutrition plan needs to support more than your protein target, and vegetables are a consistent part of how I do that.

Watch the full video for all 12 foods and the reasons I include them in my daily diet.

Whether you want to build muscle, lose body fat, or find a meal plan to get lean, the goal is to develop eating habits you can maintain. You don’t need to copy every food on my plate. Use these examples to build meals that fit your preferences, support your training, and make consistency easier.

For a structured workout program with a day-by-day meal plan, check out the ATHLEAN-X website through the link above.

Here are some of the foods I rely on every day.

My breakfast starts with egg whites. They give me a convenient source of protein without adding many calories or much fat. When your goal is to get ripped while maintaining muscle, having an easy way to include protein at breakfast helps you start the day on track. Egg whites also leave room for other foods in the meal without making it difficult to manage your overall calorie intake.

Oatmeal is another staple of my daily meal plan. It provides carbohydrates to fuel my workouts, along with fiber that helps make breakfast more satisfying. I use plain oatmeal so I can control what goes into it instead of relying on varieties with added sugar. If you’re wondering what to eat to be lean, a breakfast you enjoy and can prepare consistently is a great place to start.

I drink skim milk with breakfast and use it in my oatmeal and protein shake later in the day. It supplies protein and calcium while keeping calories lower than the same amount of whole milk. Because I consume it several times throughout the day, that difference helps me keep my diet aligned with my goals. I also choose milk fortified with vitamins A and D.

videos.title: Sam Altman’s Screenless AI Device Could Replace Your Phone
videos.summary_source_text:
Sam Altman’s Screenless AI Device Could Replace Your Phone https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

OpenAI paid roughly $6.5 billion in stock for a hardware startup with about 55 employees — around $118 million per person — and the public still hasn’t seen the device they were hired to build.

What we do know is stranger than most of the rumors. OpenAI has never officially described its first Jony Ive-designed AI device, and some of the clearest details about it only became public because of trademark and legal battles. Those court filings also directly contradict several popular claims about what OpenAI is building.

On May 21, 2025, OpenAI announced its acquisition of io Products, the hardware company founded by legendary Apple designer Jony Ive alongside former Apple designers Scott Cannon, Evans Hankey, and Tang Tan. The widely reported $6.5 billion valuation was an all-stock deal, and the acquisition closed in July 2025.

The talent involved is significant. Tang Tan, who previously led iPhone and Apple Watch design work, became OpenAI’s Chief Hardware Officer according to Apple’s lawsuit filings. Evans Hankey, Apple’s former industrial design leader, is also deeply involved, alongside a growing group of former Apple engineers and designers.

But what are they actually making?

The strongest clues came from OpenAI’s trademark dispute with AI audio company iyO. In sworn declarations, Tang Tan said the prototype is “not an in-ear device, nor a wearable device,” while Evans Hankey said there are no current plans for a custom-molded earpiece product.

That makes the widely circulated OpenAI earbud, behind-the-ear “Sweetpea,” and AI necklace rumors extremely difficult to reconcile with OpenAI’s own court filings.

Credible reporting instead points toward something screenless. Wired reported that a prototype can sit on a desk alongside a phone and laptop, while Axios reported that pocketable prototypes exist and that Sam Altman has internally described the concept as a third core device alongside your phone and laptop.

That still leaves enormous gaps. OpenAI hasn’t confirmed cameras, sensors, battery life, chipset, exact dimensions, pricing, or even the product’s final name. A voice-first interface implies microphones and some form of audio output, while heavy cloud dependence seems likely, but those remain inferences rather than announced specifications.

And hardware may be strategically important for a much bigger reason.

OpenAI is increasingly focused on AI agents that remember context, use tools, and continue working without constant prompting. Owning the hardware could give OpenAI control over the microphones, sensors, firmware, interface, and distribution layer instead of operating entirely inside ecosystems controlled by Apple and Google.

That makes OpenAI’s escalating conflict with Apple especially interesting.

In July 2026, Apple sued OpenAI, io Products, Tang Tan, and former Apple engineer Chang Liu, alleging trade-secret theft connected to OpenAI’s push into consumer hardware. OpenAI denies using stolen information, and no court had ruled on the merits at the point covered in this video. The allegations should not be confused with proven facts.

But even with billions of dollars and some of Apple’s best former designers, OpenAI faces a more fundamental challenge: making a screenless AI device people actually want.

Humane’s AI Pin already demonstrated how difficult that category can be. Cloud latency, connectivity, battery consumption, privacy, bystander consent, and basic interface questions become critical when a device is potentially always listening but has no conventional display.

How do you know when it’s listening? How do you confirm sensitive actions? What happens when connectivity disappears? And most importantly: what can this device do that your phone cannot?

Timing is becoming clearer, but only slightly. OpenAI’s Chris Lehane said the company was targeting an unveiling in the second half of 2026, while a later court filing reportedly indicated the device would not ship before the end of February 2027. That could mean a late-2026 reveal followed by customer shipments in 2027.

Until OpenAI finally shows the hardware, separate what’s confirmed from what’s merely reported — and what’s simply internet speculation.

CHAPTERS

02:53 The Apple Designers Now Inside OpenAI
04:10 How a Trademark Lawsuit Leaked the Device
05:49 What We Can Actually Say the Device Is

videos.summary_source_text:
How Iginla & Sakic Revolutionized Shooting The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Why Less Is More for Connor McDavid
videos.summary_source_text:
Why Less Is More for Connor McDavid The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Google’s Gemini Gems: Build Your Own AI Team And Save 10+ Hours Weekly
videos.summary_source_text:
Google’s Gemini Gems: Build Your Own AI Team And Save 10+ Hours Weekly https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Gemini Gems sound like persistent custom AI experts — but under the hood, they’re much simpler. They don’t automatically remember your old conversations, they don’t retrain Gemini around your preferences, and their knowledge files aren’t a live database. What they actually give you is a reusable set of instructions plus reference files that follow you into every new Gem conversation.

That distinction matters, because Gems can be genuinely useful when you understand exactly what they are — and surprisingly limiting when you expect something closer to an autonomous AI assistant.

Google introduced Gems in August 2024 as “custom AI experts for help on any topic.” Creating one doesn’t modify or fine-tune the underlying Gemini model. Instead, you define a role, tone, rules, and behavior that the Gem repeatedly applies. The result is much more consistent than rebuilding the same prompt every time, but the Gem still inherits the strengths and weaknesses of the Gemini model underneath it. If the base model can hallucinate, a carefully written Gem can too.

Knowledge files add another layer. You can give a Gem documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, images, and other supported material so it can answer using information you provide. That makes Gems useful for company policies, brand guidelines, research material, pricing information, documentation, and other specialized knowledge.

But there’s an important catch: these files are static. If a source document changes later, the Gem doesn’t automatically become a continuously synced version of that source. That difference between “attached knowledge” and “live knowledge” is one of the biggest things to understand before building around Gems.

The good news is that creating a custom Gem is now available to eligible free Gemini users, after initially being restricted to paid subscribers. Building one takes only a few minutes: name it, write the instructions, optionally attach knowledge, test it, and save it. There’s no training process or waiting period.

We put that system into practical scenarios: a research assistant designed to enforce sourcing rules, a brand and knowledge assistant grounded in uploaded information, and a code reviewer forced to follow a rigid analysis template. These examples reveal where Gems are strongest. They’re excellent at repeatedly enforcing structure, voice, rules, and reference material.

They also reveal the limitation: consistency is not the same thing as correctness.

A Gem can format a code review perfectly without actually executing the code. It can follow strict research instructions while still depending on the capabilities of the underlying model. And attached knowledge can ground its answers without turning the Gem into a continuously learning assistant.

Sharing adds another interesting dimension. Gems can be shared with other users, and permissions can determine whether someone simply uses the Gem or can edit it. But sharing also raises questions around instructions, attached source material, permissions, and what recipients can actually access.

Then there’s the bigger limitation: Gems still aren’t autonomous agents. Features available elsewhere in the Gemini ecosystem don’t automatically become capabilities of every traditional Gem. That means you need to distinguish between a reusable instruction-based assistant and the more structured workflow capabilities Google is developing through systems such as Opal.

And there’s another assistant story that makes this much more interesting.

According to the developments covered in this video, OpenAI is moving away from Custom GPTs and toward a plugin-based system, creating a very different migration problem for people who have already built workflows around custom assistants. Instructions and knowledge may have a path forward, while other elements can require rebuilding.

Put the two approaches side by side and you get a revealing picture of where custom AI assistants are heading: reusable prompts and knowledge are valuable, but the industry increasingly wants assistants that can connect to tools, workflows, and real actions.

So are Gemini Gems worth using?

For a narrow, repeatable job — research formatting, brand knowledge, specialized instructions, structured reviews, or a consistent voice — they can be extremely practical. But if you expect a Gem to remember everything about you, continuously update its knowledge, or behave like a fully autonomous agent, you’re asking it to be something it currently isn’t.

This video breaks down exactly where that line sits.

05:26 Building One Takes About Five Minutes

09:55 What Gems Still Can't Do
11:05 The Other Assistant Story Worth Knowing
12:50 The Verdict

Round 4 Highlights | 2026 Alfred Dunhill Links Championship Highlights from the final round of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship on the Old Course at St Andrews.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

First held in 2001, this year marks the 25th anniversary of a tournament that celebrates links golf at its finest. Held across the Old Course at St Andrews, Carnoustie, and Kingsbarns with the final round being played at the Old Course at The Home of Golf. Robert MacIntyre returns to defend his title he won just seven days after starring in Team Europe’s Ryder Cup win at Bethpage Black, where he became the fourth winner to hail from Scotland. Players from 28 different nations are making the journey to Scotland. Among them is an incredible line of Major Champions including Justin Rose, Matt Fitzpatrick, Bubba Watson and Brooks Koepka who is looking to become the first American winner of this tournament. Joining them is a star-studded line-up including Tommy Fleetwood, Sepp Straka and Tyrrell Hatton. With the top three ranked players on the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World not teeing it up this week, an opportunity is presented to those further down the standings as we draw nearer to the DP World Tour Play-Offs. Unlike most events on the DP World Tour, the championship includes an individual professional tournament featuring a field of 168 players along with a team championship in which each professional is paired with an amateur.

videos.title: Struggling with inconsistency... Change what your hands are doing 👀
videos.summary_source_text:
Struggling with inconsistency... Change what your hands are doing 👀 If you’re struggling with inconsistent ball striking, chunks, thin shots, or a golf swing that feels all arms, look down before you start changing what your hands are doing. 👀⛳️

Your pressure shift might be the missing piece.
Watch the feet and hips closely in this video, because the important part isn’t just where your weight goes, it’s when it gets there.

In the backswing, pressure loads into the trail side, staying more toward the inside of the trail foot rather than drifting to the outside.

But here’s the part a lot of golfers miss:
You don’t wait until the backswing is finished to start moving toward the target.
As the club is finishing the backswing, pressure is already beginning to move toward the lead side.

That gives you a better opportunity to rotate through the shot instead of:
→ Hanging back on your trail foot
→ Sliding through impact
→ Throwing the arms at the ball
→ Trying to save the strike at the last second

Think of the sequence as:
LOAD → SHIFT → ROTATE

Not:
LOAD → WAIT → PANIC. 😅

And this is why simply watching weight-shift videos can only get you so far.
You may understand exactly what you’re supposed to do and still have no idea whether you’re actually doing it.

That’s the problem the Ball First Board is designed to solve.

It gives you physical feedback for the trail-side load, helps prevent excessive sway, and gives you a reference for moving into the lead side so you can train the movement you’re seeing in this video instead of guessing.

If you’re tired of knowing what a good golf swing should look like but struggling to reproduce the feeling, this is where I’d start.

videos.title: OpenAI’s Dots: The Always-On AI Assistant Built to Handle Everything
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s Dots: The Always-On AI Assistant Built to Handle Everything https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

OpenAI just gave ChatGPT its own computer — an always-on cloud machine that can work on your goals even when you’re not actively chatting with it.

Announced at DevDay on September 29, 2026, OpenAI calls it a “Dot.” Instead of behaving like another ChatGPT session, a Dot is designed to hold ongoing responsibilities: monitoring connected apps, working across sessions, running code, browsing websites, and proactively messaging you when something needs attention.

But the bigger story is what OpenAI deliberately won’t let it do without you.

Each Dot runs on GPT-6 Astra and gets a dedicated cloud virtual machine with a Chromium browser, filesystem, and access to Codex for coding tasks. OpenAI says it can connect to more than 4,000 apps through the existing ChatGPT integration ecosystem, including Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Notion, and Salesforce.

The persistence is what makes this different. Files can remain on the Dot’s machine, connected login sessions carry over, and recurring tasks can keep running without you repeatedly issuing the same prompt. The Dot can also carry context across supported surfaces such as ChatGPT, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.

OpenAI demonstrated what that looks like with several scenarios.

One Dot noticed its user working late, found dinner options, and proactively messaged them. Another detected a mobile checkout bug, accessed the connected GitHub repository, wrote a fix, ran tests, and opened a pull request. Another identified a scheduling conflict and prepared a reschedule. A research example showed a Dot automatically rerunning an analysis whenever new experimental data arrived.

These were curated OpenAI demonstrations, though — not independent stress tests.

And that's where the permission system becomes important.

OpenAI says every planned action passes through an auto-review layer. A Dot may be allowed to handle lower-risk work within its granted permissions, but sensitive actions such as purchases, password changes, and software installation remain with the user. Custom Rules can further define exactly what an individual Dot is allowed or forbidden to do.

That architecture also matters for prompt injection. A persistent agent reading webpages and emails creates a different security problem from a chatbot answering a single prompt. OpenAI says background reading uses restricted tools and planned actions still pass through its review system, but how that protection performs against real-world attacks remains something independent testing will need to establish.

There’s another problem: persistent mistakes.

A bad ChatGPT answer might disappear into an old conversation. A bad assumption made by an agent working independently for several days could influence multiple later actions before a human notices. OpenAI acknowledges Dots can make mistakes and says they can stop and ask for help when authentication expires, a website fails, or safety monitoring intervenes.

Not everything underneath Dots is completely new, either. Browser automation builds on ideas already seen in Operator, coding uses Codex, and thousands of integrations already existed. The major change is packaging those capabilities around a persistent identity, dedicated cloud computer, recurring responsibilities, and an action-review system.

OpenAI has also discussed a future involving teams of specialized Dots coordinating with each other. That isn't the product shipping today.

The launch has significant limitations: one Dot per account, ChatGPT Pro or Business Premium access in eligible markets, no public API, unspecified compute and memory limits, and Codex-heavy workloads still counting against normal usage limits. The script cites ChatGPT Pro at $100 per month.

So is this really “AI that never stops”?

Dots can act between conversations without waiting for another prompt, which is a meaningful change. But they're still operating inside boundaries established by a human, with sensitive actions requiring approval.

The interesting question isn't whether OpenAI has created a fully autonomous digital employee. It's what happens when an AI assistant stops being something you repeatedly ask for help — and starts holding a responsibility over time.

The launch has significant limitations: one Dot per account, ChatGPT Pro or Business Premium access in eligible markets, no public API, unspecified compute and memory limits, and Codex-heavy workloads still counting against normal usage limits. The script cites ChatGPT Pro at $100 per month.

So is this really “AI that never stops”?

Dots can act between conversations without waiting for another prompt, which is a meaningful change. But they're still operating inside boundaries established by a human, with sensitive actions requiring approval.

The interesting question isn't whether OpenAI has created a fully autonomous digital employee. It's what happens when an AI assistant stops being something you repeatedly ask for help — and starts holding a responsibility over time.

Moving the arms and body together as one unit is the single most common reason golfers can't hit their driver farther — and most of them are trying to fix it by getting more body rotation, which makes it worse. Eric Cogorno breaks down the three driver drills he has been giving to students to fix this exact pattern: learning to get golf club head speed out of the arms and hands first, then rehinging and rotating through the ball the way the Rory McIlroy driver swing demonstrates, and finally using front end therapy to preset the correct follow through position and ingrain it into a real swing. These driver swing tips have produced an effortless golf swing feel and significant distance gains for golfers of all handicaps. If you leave this video without trying the alignment rod impact bag drill, you're leaving club head speed and effortless driver distance on the table.

What You'll Learn:
• Why moving the arms and body together as one unit kills golf club head speed and causes pulls and fades with driver
• The alignment rod and impact bag drill for training arm speed independent of the body — three with lead hand, three with trail hand, three together
• Why the lead side needs to slow down and break for the arms and hands to generate real golf club head speed
• How the Rory McIlroy driver swing demonstrates the correct rehinge and rotate position through the ball
• The lead arm only drill: butt of club down, elbow down, glove logo down — how to train the correct golf follow through
• Why toe passing heel through impact closes the club face and reduces the fade for golfers who slice or miss right
• Frontend therapy: how to preset the correct follow through position and swing back through it for a more effortless golf swing
• How to increase driver distance by using arms and hands as the primary speed source — not body rotation

How to ACTUALLY Lose Belly Fat (When All Else Fails) Dealing with stubborn belly fat? Find out why you’re struggling to lose belly fat despite doing everything right, plus how to lose belly fat by finally addressing the root cause.

0:17 Belly fat explained

2:58 20-hour fasting for weight loss and stubborn belly fat

3:43 What is a HIIT workout?

https://youtu.be/zA3Np51HLjE

Our bodies have evolved to store body fat around the midsection as a survival mechanism. There are 9 times more receptors for fat storage than fat burning in this area. Adrenaline helps activate the fat-burning process, which can help shift the body from storing belly fat to burning it.

High insulin levels can prevent you from losing belly fat. Fasting for 20 hours a day can help lower insulin to your baseline. A HIIT workout during your fast can significantly increase adrenaline to boost belly fat loss. Weight training combined with HIIT can stimulate even more adrenaline.

To reduce visceral fat, it’s critical to lower insulin, which is why 20-hour fasting can be a powerful way to stimulate visceral fat loss.

There are also more cortisol receptors around the midsection than in other areas of the body, so chronic stress could be another reason you’re having trouble losing belly fat. Adequate sleep, sunlight exposure, and avoiding food for three hours before bed are also important for losing belly fat.

If you want to lose belly fat, it’s vital to avoid industrial palm oil, seed oils, sugar, and starches.
